title: The Terraces and the Three Crops

collection.credit:
NEW EVENTS - LIVING CULTURE VII: KNOWLEDGE, CONSENT AND SHARED WORK (LCG-01..50, draft, 2026-11-18)
From the owner's Volume III concepts (201-300): weather readers and navigators, seed keepers and terrace builders, permission and consent, who leads and who is heard, homes built by many hands, songs for the uncelebrated, and a village writing its own story.
Written in the style of the owner's own events. The owner waived the review ("I'm sure the draft events are fine"); every event passed the Isola rules and the final 15-point review, logged in the notes.

collection.description: Farmers want to repair the old hillside terraces and try planting three crops together: repair them, or start simpler gardens.

setup.name: The setup
setup.text: The old terraces on the hillside are crumbling. (subject) wants to rebuild them stone by stone and plant three crops together the way the old farmers did: beans climbing the stalks, squash leaves shading the soil. (friend) says flat gardens by the stream would be quicker. What should they do?

o1.name: Outcome A
o1.text: It takes a whole season to rebuild the walls. The first planting is a tangle of beans, stalks and squash, and (friend) thinks it looks a mess. Then the harvest comes, and it is the best the hillside has given in living memory.

o2.name: Outcome B
o2.text: The stream gardens are planted in a month and grow quickly. Then the stream floods and washes half of them away. (friend) helps (subject) start on the terraces after all.
